headline: Chips Carry the Tape as Rate Worries Hit Homebuilders
body_html:
Stocks are leaning higher in Wednesday's session so far, with 386 of the 668 names we track advancing and 275 declining. Prices are still moving and are not final. Chips are doing the heavy lifting: our semiconductor group is up 3.84%, well clear of every other corner of the market.

Financials are up 1.3%, energy 1.15% and software 0.8%, while healthcare (0.53%) and industrials (0.38%) are modestly firmer. Homebuilders are the weak spot, down 0.94%, after mortgage rates climbed sharply following four weeks of easing. Consumer shares are slightly lower, off 0.28%. Azenta is the standout, up 12.46%, while Applied Optoelectronics, Bloom Energy and Sandisk are each up about 10%. Tokyo Electron, down 4.16%, is a notable exception among chip names.

Into the close, watch whether semiconductor leadership holds or fades, and how oil trades on Iran headlines after a gain of about 1% on word that nuclear material will stay in the country. Rate-sensitive homebuilders also bear watching. The next session is Thursday, November 12.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors Set the Pace
briefs.body: The semiconductor group is up 3.84% in the session so far, the strongest showing among the nine sectors we track. Sandisk is up 9.82% and MaxLinear 7.75%, while Applied Optoelectronics has gained 10.3%. Prices are not final, so the lead could narrow by the close.

briefs.headline: Mortgage Rates Jump, Homebuilders Slip
briefs.body: Mortgage rates rose sharply after four straight weeks of easing, and homebuilders are the weakest sector at down 0.94%. The move shows how quickly housing-linked shares react to borrowing costs. Any further climb in rates could keep pressure on the group into the close.

briefs.headline: Oil Firms on Iran Nuclear Stance
briefs.body: Oil is up about 1% after Iran's security chief said enriched nuclear material will not leave the country. Energy shares are up 1.15% as a group. Bloom Energy, a fuel-cell maker, is up 10.22%, one of the day's biggest gains among the stocks we track.

briefs.headline: Gulf Markets Hold Gains, Shipping Fears Linger
briefs.body: Gulf equities edged higher on hopes that the pause in the Iran conflict will hold. Concerns about shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have not gone away, though. Traders will be watching for any shift in tone that could change risk appetite late in the session.

briefs.headline: Shoppers Spend, but Strain Is Showing
briefs.body: A retail monitor from CNBC and the National Retail Federation shows consumers still spending while signs of pressure build. Our consumer group is down 0.28% in the session so far. Premium food name Vital Farms is the day's weakest mover, off 4.85%.

briefs.headline: Azenta Leads a Mixed Healthcare Tape
briefs.body: Healthcare is up 0.53% as a group, but moves under the surface are wide. Life-science tools company Azenta is the session's top gainer at 12.46%. Eye-care firm Alcon is down 4.49%, among the largest decliners we track.
